detail: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation: Δv = Isp × g₀ × ln(m₀ / mf), with g₀ = 9.80665 m/s². It is the same equation every real rocket is designed with.
Inverse-square law: power ÷ distance². Mars gets about 43% of Earth's sunlight, Jupiter about 3.7%.
Light takes 8.317 minutes to cross one AU, so the delay is the distance in AU × 8.317 minutes each way.

what: Where the spacecraft is on the map
detail: A Hohmann transfer half-ellipse, timed with Kepler's equation, so the spacecraft really does move fast near the Sun and slowly far away.
Mars lines up with Earth about every 26 months, Jupiter about every 13. The Moon needs no window at all.
Rounded from real mission durations: about 3 days to the Moon, 8 months to Mars, 5 years to Jupiter.
Chemical engines really do reach about 320 seconds and ion engines about 3000, which is why an ion engine needs so little fuel.

what: The real missions we compare you with
detail: Chandrayaan-2, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Mangalyaan, MAVEN, Juno and Galileo, with their real agencies and launch years.

what: The stories on the challenge cards
detail: Every "Real story" line is something that happened to a real spacecraft, with the year it happened.
Chosen to make the choices interesting and the numbers easy to hold in your head. A real spacecraft part list is far longer.
$250M, $150M and $900M. Real missions cost more, but the shape of the choice is the same: every kilogram costs money.
A made-up score for what each instrument is worth, so missions can be compared. Real science is not a number.
Tuned so a careful design usually survives and a tight one sometimes does not. The events themselves are real kinds of trouble.

what: How much a challenge costs you
detail: The fuel, science and power a choice costs are game values, picked so no single card can end a well-built mission on its own.
